climate.overview_html: The day’s new diplomatic signal: an early speakers’ list for the COP31 World Leaders’ Summit (Antalya, 11–12 November) shows only 77 heads of state or government registered — nearly a third fewer than the 116 who spoke at COP28 in Dubai. France, Germany, Italy, India, Russia, Canada and Japan do not appear on the current list; China is expected to send Vice-Premier Ding Xuexiang rather than President Xi Jinping. Former UN climate chief Yvo de Boer called it a poor signal: “climate action needs a strong show of support, not empty seats at a leaders’ summit.” The attendance drop lands against the backdrop of the UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2026 (21 October), which declared that the 1.5°C no-or-limited-overshoot pathway is lost and current policies track to 2.6–2.8°C. Australia’s Chris Bowen has appointed 10 co-facilitators across five ministerial pairs, and Turkey’s presidency has confirmed 159 pavilions — but with G7 leaders largely absent, the ambition gap between the UNEP scenarios and COP31’s likely outcomes is widening ahead of the 9 November opening.

items.headline: Only 77 Leaders Registered to Speak at COP31 World Leaders’ Summit — Down a Third from COP28’s 116; France, Germany, Italy, India, Canada, Japan Absent; Former UN Climate Chief Calls Low Turnout a “Poor Signal”
items.summary: An early provisional UN speakers' list shows only 77 heads of state or government registered to address the COP31 World Leaders' Summit in Antalya on November 11–12 — down from 116 at COP28 in Dubai and 144 at COP27 in Sharm el-Sheikh. Notable absentees include the leaders of France, Germany, Italy, India, Russia, Canada and Japan. China is expected to be represented by Vice-Premier Ding Xuexiang rather than President Xi Jinping. Brazilian President Lula and Australian Prime Minister Albanese are confirmed. Former UN climate secretariat chief Yvo de Boer said 'climate action needs a strong show of support, not empty seats at a leaders' summit'. The Turkish COP31 presidency has separately said it expects 85 world leaders; the difference likely reflects leaders who attend but do not take a formal speaking slot.

items.source: UNEP / DownToEarth / Nature News / NatureWorldNews / GreentechLead
items.headline: UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2026 “The Point of Return”: 1.5°C Overshoot Now Inevitable; Global Emissions Flat at 58.4 GtCO<sub>2</sub>e in 2025; Current Policies Track to 2.6–2.8°C; Lowest-Overshoot Path Needs 18% Cuts by 2030, 45% by 2035, 69% by 2040; US Leads G20 Emissions Rise
items.summary: UNEP's annual Emissions Gap Report, released October 21 and titled 'The Point of Return', officially declares that the opportunity to limit warming to 1.5°C with 'no or limited' overshoot has been lost. Global GHG emissions were approximately 58.4 GtCO₂e in 2025 — essentially unchanged from a revised 58.5 GtCO₂e in 2024 — as a fall in land-use and wildfire emissions offset continued growth in fossil CO₂. Existing NDCs, if fully implemented, would cut emissions by only 5–8% by 2030 and 11–15% by 2035; a lowest-possible-overshoot path that peaks warming at 1.7–1.8°C before returning to 1.5°C by century's end requires cuts of 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035, and 69% by 2040, plus removal of approximately 320 Gt CO₂ from the atmosphere. Under current policies, warming reaches 2.6–2.8°C. Among G20 nations, the US logged the largest emissions increase (+133 Mt CO₂e), driven by rising electricity demand and a coal rebound. Solar PV capacity has grown seven times faster than projected since Paris, and renewable electricity capacity has tripled faster than anticipated.

items.headline: COP31 Names 10 Co-Facilitators to Steer Key Climate Talks in Antalya: Australia’s Bowen Appoints Five Ministerial Pairs Covering Finance, Adaptation, Mitigation, Just Transition and Oceans; Turkey Expects 85 World Leaders, Record 159 Pavilions
items.summary: Australian Climate Change Minister Chris Bowen announced on October 21–22 that ten senior representatives — five ministerial pairs — will co-facilitate the key negotiating tracks at Antalya: (1) climate finance and the Baku Finance Goal, (2) adaptation and the Global Goal on Adaptation, (3) mitigation and NDC implementation, (4) just transition, and (5) oceans and coastal ecosystems. Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum said Turkey expects 85 world leaders at the World Leaders' Summit, with a record 159 pavilions and 90 delegation offices approved. Xinhua reported that the Turkish co-presidency is framing COP31 as a 'policies implementation' summit, seeking to operationalise the Baku Finance Goal, the Loss and Damage Fund, and Article 6 carbon markets.

items.headline: China Sets COP31 Antalya Priorities: Demands Detailed Roadmap for US$300 Billion Annual Climate Finance Goal, Opposes Carbon Border Mechanisms as Trade Barriers, Pledges to Speak for Developing Nations
items.summary: China's Vice Minister of Ecology and Environment Li Gao published Beijing's COP31 positions on October 21–22. Top priorities: (1) compelling developed countries to deliver a concrete implementation roadmap for the US$300 billion annual climate finance goal agreed at COP29; (2) opposing the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism as a violation of UNFCCC common-but-differentiated responsibilities; (3) demanding the global stocktake focus on implementation gaps in developed-nation commitments; (4) tripling adaptation finance. China intends to attend at the highest level. The positions set up a significant clash with the EU at Antalya.

items.headline: UN Secretary-General Guterres: World Falling “Dangerously Short” on Climate Action Ahead of COP31; El Niño and Record Heat Amplify Urgency
items.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres issued a statement on October 21 calling the world 'dangerously short' on climate action, referencing record-breaking heat, devastating floods, and an unprecedented El Niño as making accelerated action 'ever more urgent.' A concurrent UN release emphasised that the NCQG agreed at COP29 must be operationalised and that the UNFCCC process faces a credibility crisis with climate-vulnerable nations. With COP31 in Antalya opening November 9, diplomatic pressure is intensifying.

items.headline: South Africa at COP31: As Climate Shocks Intensify, Pretoria Pushes for Substantially More Adaptation Finance; Aligns with G77 Demand to Triple Adaptation Funding by 2035
items.summary: South Africa is entering COP31 with adaptation finance as its top priority, arguing that developing nations most vulnerable to climate shocks have been shortchanged in NCQG negotiations dominated by mitigation framing. South Africa aligns with G77 demands for adaptation finance to be tripled by 2035, mirroring the European Parliament's October resolution position. While adaptation funding pledges have grown, actual disbursements remain far below commitments — a structural issue the African Group plans to press at Antalya.

major_events.name: Typhoon Champi (Rosal) — Track Converges on Kyushu, Japan; Taiwan Island-Wide Shutdown Lifted 24 Oct; 980 hPa / 108 kph Sustained / 162 kph Gusts; JMA Forecasts Kyushu Approach ~Oct 26, Extratropical Transition Oct 27
major_events.status: As of 24 Oct morning: Champi is traveling north of Okinawa’s Sakishima Islands. Taiwan’s island-wide shutdown (schools, stock exchange, government) from 23 Oct has been lifted as the storm passed without a direct Taiwan landfall. Current JMA intensity: 980 hPa central pressure, 108 kph sustained winds, 162 kph gusts — significantly weaker than the Oct 22 peak of 900 hPa at Category 5 equivalent over the Philippine Sea. The JMA, JTWC, and Korea Meteorological Administration have converged on a Kyushu approach track: closest passage to southwestern Japan expected ~Monday 26 October, followed by extratropical transition south of Honshu by Tuesday 27 October. Track uncertainty cone grows to ±185 km by 25 Oct; JTWC rates both track and intensity confidence as low. A Korean forecast notes some residual risk of the subtropical high pushing the storm westward toward the Taiwan Strait instead.
major_events.impact: Japan: JMA heavy rain advisories issued for northern Kyushu, Chugoku, Kinki, and Hokuriku regions through Monday; land warnings expected as approach nears. Taiwan: post-passage assessment underway; island-wide shutdown lifted; 600+ flight cancellations being cleared. China: Zhejiang and Fujian heavy rain warnings continuing. Korea: rain and wind expected in southern regions (Jeju) through weekend.

major_events.name: SE Asian Peatland Haze (Indonesia/Borneo/Sumatra) — Day 27+ — Satellite Monitoring Active; ~1.9 Million Hectares Burned; Monsoon Onset Expected Late Oct – Nov; ASMC Level 3 Alert Continues
major_events.status: As of 24 Oct: Satellite technology actively deployed to track peat fire hotspots via thermal anomaly detection (Manila Times, 24 Oct). Forecasters expect gradual monsoon onset across Sumatra and Kalimantan in late October and November, offering the first realistic suppression pathway — but rewetting deep peat will lag weeks behind rainfall onset. An Oct 23 op-ed (Eurasia Review) notes structural ASEAN enforcement failures drive recurrence. ASMC Level 3 alert remains in force. No significant change to the fire extent or health burden data from 23 Oct.
major_events.impact: Indonesia: 283,270+ respiratory illness cases (7 provinces); protests demanding national disaster declaration ongoing. Malaysia: schools closed in affected states; parliament discussing air purifier tax rebates. Singapore: Transboundary Haze Pollution Act enforcement notices to plantation operators. ~40 million people exposed 2+ months across Kalimantan and Sumatra. Super El Niño + positive IOD continue to suppress monsoon rainfall.

weather.overview_html: The dominant story on 24 October is Typhoon Champi’s track shift. JMA, JTWC and the Korea Meteorological Administration have converged on a Kyushu approach around Monday 26 October, as Champi — now at 980 hPa, 108 kph sustained, 162 kph gusts — passes north of Okinawa’s Sakishima Islands after Taiwan avoided a direct landfall. Taiwan’s island-wide shutdown (schools, stock exchange, 600+ flights) has been lifted. JMA-based Weathernews guidance puts the storm at tropical-storm strength (996 hPa) by 00 UTC Oct 26, with extratropical transition south of Honshu by Oct 27. Heavy rain advisories cover northern Kyushu, Chugoku, Kinki and Hokuriku; JTWC rates both track and intensity confidence as low. On the SE Asian haze crisis (day 27+), satellite thermal anomaly monitoring is now being actively deployed to track smouldering peat hotspots; an Eurasia Review analysis (23 Oct) finds ASEAN structural enforcement gaps drive recurrence regardless of the improving forecast for late-October monsoon onset.

items.headline: Typhoon Champi 24 Oct: Track Converges on Kyushu Approach ~Oct 26; Taiwan Shutdown Lifted; 980 hPa / 108 kph Sustained; Extratropical Transition Forecast Oct 27; JMA Issues Heavy Rain Advisories Northern Kyushu, Chugoku, Kinki, Hokuriku
items.summary: By October 24, JMA, JTWC, and the Korea Meteorological Administration had converged on a Kyushu approach track for Typhoon Champi, with the closest passage to southwestern Japan expected around Monday morning October 26. The storm is then forecast to recurve northeast and undergo extratropical transition south of Honshu by Tuesday October 27. Current intensity (09:00 JST Oct 24): 980 hPa central pressure, 108 kph sustained winds, 162 kph gusts — a dramatic weakening from the 900 hPa peak over the Philippine Sea. Taiwan's island-wide shutdown from October 23 was lifted as the storm passed the northeast coast without a direct landfall. JMA issued heavy rain advisories for northern Kyushu, the Chugoku and Kinki regions, and the Hokuriku coast through Monday. Track uncertainty: ±55 km at 00 UTC October 24, growing to ±185 km by October 25 and ±370 km by October 27. JTWC rates both track and intensity confidence as low. A Korean forecast noted the subtropical high could push the storm westward toward the Taiwan Strait, preserving some alternative-track risk.

items.headline: SE Asian Peatland Haze Day 27+: Satellites Deployed to Track Indonesian Peat Fire Hotspots via Thermal Anomaly; Monsoon Onset Expected Late Oct–Nov; ASEAN Structural Enforcement Gaps Persist
items.summary: On October 24, the Manila Times reported that satellite thermal anomaly detection is being actively deployed to track Indonesian peat fire hotspots — capable of pinpointing smouldering areas underground where surface fires appear extinguished but combustion continues. Meteorologists expect gradual monsoon onset across Sumatra and Kalimantan in late October and November, offering the first realistic pathway to suppressing active fires; however, rewetting deep peat will lag weeks behind rainfall onset. An October 23 Eurasia Review op-ed analysed why the transboundary haze crisis persists despite decades of ASEAN cooperation, concluding that structural enforcement failures and unchanged land-use incentives are the core drivers. ASMC Level 3 alert remains in force; Singapore has invoked the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act against plantation operators.

renewables.overview_html: Four developments from 22 October broaden this week’s renewables picture. Applied Digital and Soluna Holdings signed a definitive agreement for a 50 MW AI data centre in Briscoe County, Texas, co-located with the 150 MW Briscoe Wind Farm — one of the clearest examples yet of AI compute infrastructure co-locating directly on wind assets to absorb curtailment. On the same day, Mumbai’s BEST utility approved a 25-year, 220 MW solar-plus-storage PPA with India’s SECI at ‹2.86/kWh, and Acciona Energía brought two Croatian wind farms (72 MW combined) into commercial operation under 12-year Contracts for Difference. ENGIE broke ground on the Buisson solar-plus-storage project in France (29.8 MWp + 8.8 MW / 20 MWh BESS). The week’s larger-scale anchors remain China Huaneng’s 960 MW wind-solar-storage hybrid full grid connection in Inner Mongolia and the Atmos / BayWa r.e. Australian portfolio acquisition pushing 2 GW.

items.headline: Applied Digital and Soluna Holdings Sign Definitive Agreement for 50 MW AI Data Centre at Briscoe County, Texas, Co-Located with 150 MW Briscoe Wind Farm; Wind + Grid Hybrid Power Supply for AI Compute
items.summary: Applied Digital Corporation and Soluna Holdings signed a definitive agreement to jointly develop a 50 MW AI data centre in Briscoe County, Texas. The facility will be co-located adjacent to the 150 MW Briscoe Wind Farm and draw power from a combination of wind generation and grid electricity, designed to absorb curtailment periods while providing firm compute capacity for AI workloads. The deal is one of a growing cohort of AI data centre projects seeking co-location with renewable generation to reduce grid interconnect costs and carbon intensity.

items.headline: Mumbai BEST Utility Approves 220 MW Solar-Plus-Storage PPA with India’s Solar Energy Corporation (SECI) at ‹2.86/kWh for 25 Years
items.summary: Mumbai's electricity distribution utility BEST (Brihanmumbai Electric Supply and Transport) approved a 25-year power purchase agreement with India's Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) for 220 MW of solar-plus-battery storage at a tariff of ₹2.86 per kWh. The procurement adds firm renewable capacity to one of India's highest-density urban electricity networks, leveraging SECI's competitive procurement process. The deal continues a pattern of Indian state utilities seeking long-term renewable PPAs ahead of rising demand from electrification and data centre growth.

items.headline: Acciona Energía Brings Two Croatian Wind Farms (72 MW Combined) into Commercial Operation, Backed by 12-Year Contracts for Difference; Eurus Energy + Tohoku Electric Start Building 33.6 MW Fukui Kunimi Wind Farm in Japan
items.summary: Acciona Energía started commercial operation of two wind farms in Croatia with a combined capacity of 72 MW, supported by 12-year Contracts for Difference awarded through Croatia's national renewable energy procurement programme. In the same GreentechLead roundup, Eurus Energy and Tohoku Electric Power were reported to have started construction of the 33.6 MW Fukui Kunimi Wind Farm in Japan (construction commenced September 28, formally announced October 21). Both projects are part of accelerating renewable buildout across Europe and Asia-Pacific ahead of national decarbonisation targets.

items.headline: ENGIE Breaks Ground on Buisson Solar-Plus-Storage Project in France: 29.8 MWp Solar + 8.8 MW / 20 MWh BESS; Colocation Model
items.summary: ENGIE has begun construction of the Buisson solar-plus-storage project in France, combining 29.8 MWp of photovoltaic generation with an 8.8 MW / 20 MWh battery energy storage system. The colocation model allows the battery to capture excess solar output during peak generation and shift it to evening demand, reducing curtailment and improving project economics. The Buisson project is part of ENGIE's French solar pipeline, which has accelerated under France's repowering and greenfield procurement rounds.

items.source: PV Magazine Australia / Baker McKenzie / Enerdata / Power Technology
items.headline: Atmos Renewables Acquires BayWa r.e.’s Australian Renewable Portfolio — Yatpool Solar (106 MW), Hughenden Solar (20 MW), Bullawah Wind Development (~800 MW) — Pushing Total Capacity Beyond 2 GW; BayWa Retreats to Core European Markets
items.summary: Atmos Renewables, the renewable energy arm of Igneo Infrastructure Partners, finalised on October 16 the acquisition of a portfolio of Australian renewable assets from BayWa r.e. The acquired assets include: Yatpool Solar Park (106 MW, Victoria, operating since 2021); Hughenden Solar Park (20 MW, Queensland, operating since 2018); and the Bullawah Wind Farm development in New South Wales (~800 MW wind plus 359 MW/718 MWh BESS per Enerdata). The deal pushes Atmos's combined operating and in-construction capacity beyond 2 GW. BayWa r.e. is retreating from non-core markets amid its parent company's financial restructuring. Baker McKenzie advised BayWa; purchase price was not disclosed.

items.headline: China Huaneng Fully Grid-Connects 960 MW Wind-Solar-Storage Hybrid in Inner Mongolia: 810 MW Wind + 150 MW Solar + 60 MW/240 MWh Grid-Forming BESS + Coal Flexible Dispatch; First Integrated Coal-Renewables Retrofit of This Scale in China
items.summary: China Huaneng announced the full grid connection of a 960 MW wind-solar-storage project at Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia, comprising 810 MW wind, 150 MW solar PV, a 60 MW/240 MWh grid-forming BESS, and a 20 Mvar STATCOM, paired with a coal-fired plant in flexible dispatch mode. Described as the first project of this kind in China, expected annual output is approximately 2.3 billion kWh. Ulanqab is a key hub for ultra-high-voltage transmission lines connecting Inner Mongolia to coastal load centres.

items.headline: AMEA Power Signs Agreements for 250 MW/1,000 MWh Battery Storage Project in Uzbekistan’s Bukhara Region; Central Asia’s Largest Battery Commitment of 2026
items.summary: UAE-based AMEA Power signed project agreements on October 16 for a 250 MW / 1,000 MWh BESS in Uzbekistan's Bukhara region (Gijduvan district). It follows AMEA Power's existing 150 MW / 300 MWh BESS under construction near Tashkent (ground broken May 2026). Combined, AMEA Power's total committed Uzbekistan storage is 400 MW / 1,300 MWh. No deal price was disclosed.

items.headline: EirGrid Data: 15% of Ireland’s Wind Electricity Wasted H1 2026 Due to Grid Constraints; Enough to Power 667,000 Homes; 13%+ of All Renewables Curtailed First Nine Months; Grid Investment Lag Worsening
items.summary: EirGrid figures reveal that more than 13% of available wind and solar electricity in Ireland during the first nine months of 2026 could not be used due to grid constraints. In H1 alone, 15% of wind electricity was dispatched down — enough to power approximately 667,000 Irish homes — worsening from 2025 curtailment rates. Experts cite a multi-year lag between accelerating renewable capacity additions and major transmission infrastructure investment, with Grid West and the North-South interconnector still years from completion.

items.headline: Foresight Energy Infrastructure Partners II Completes Acquisition of Nivala BESS — Finland’s Largest Battery Energy Storage System — from Fotowatio Renewable Ventures; Nordic Grid-Balancing Assets Draw Continued Institutional Capital
items.summary: Foresight Energy Infrastructure Partners II completed its acquisition of 100% of Nivala BESS — Finland's largest battery energy storage system — from Fotowatio Renewable Ventures (FRV), the renewables subsidiary of Abdul Latif Jameel. No deal price was disclosed. Nivala provides frequency and voltage grid-balancing services in Finland's electricity market, where curtailment pressure from growing intermittent renewable capacity is rising. The acquisition continues a trend of institutional infrastructure funds acquiring operational Nordic BESS assets as ancillary services revenue models mature.

science.overview_html: New this window: arXiv:2610.22555 (c. 15 October) presents an AI foundation model for atmospheric chemistry and climate that achieves R2 > 0.85 on 23 of 27 predicted fields while running ~100× faster than the physics-based UKCA model — a significant milestone for making atmospheric chemistry tractable in high-resolution earth-system simulations. DWD’s AICON-Global (arXiv:2608.24651; data publicly available since March 2026) has now completed one year of verification, performing competitively with the operational ICON NWP system for surface variables at short-to-medium range, with noted damping of mesoscale activity. Active Typhoon Champi sharpens the relevance of arXiv:2610.22077, which finds AI models beat ECMWF IFS-ENS on tropical cyclone track but remain weak on intensity and ensemble spread — exactly the failure modes visible in Champi’s approach uncertainty. arXiv:2610.26145 (NeurIPS 2026 workshop, 20 Oct) addresses the complementary downscaling challenge for hourly precipitation at sub-km scales. The Mouatadid et al. Nature paper on probabilistic bias correction that doubles AI subseasonal skill remains the landmark publication of the period.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.22555 — AI Foundation Model for Atmospheric Chemistry and Climate: R<sup>2</sup> > 0.85 on 23/27 Fields; ~100× Faster than UKCA; Enables Tractable High-Resolution Chemistry-Climate Simulation
items.summary: This paper presents an AI foundation model for atmospheric chemistry and climate. The model predicts 27 atmospheric chemistry and climate fields; 23 of 27 achieve R² above 0.85 against reference simulations. It runs approximately 100 times faster than the UK Chemistry and Aerosols (UKCA) physics-based model, making high-resolution atmospheric chemistry tractable within earth-system model ensembles or large-scale climate projections. Atmospheric chemistry — governing aerosol formation, ozone, and reactive trace gas budgets — is among the most computationally expensive components of coupled earth-system models; an emulator at this accuracy threshold opens the door to routine inclusion in AI-driven climate projection pipelines.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.26145 — Hourly Precipitation Downscaling from km-Scale Regional Climate Simulations (Addison, Kendon, Watson); Accepted to NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Tackling Climate Change with Machine Learning
items.meta: Addison, Kendon, Watson · arXiv:2610.26145 [physics.ao-ph] · 20 Oct 2026 · NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Tackling Climate Change with Machine Learning
items.summary: Henry Addison, Elizabeth Kendon and Peter Watson present a deep-learning approach to downscaling hourly precipitation from kilometre-scale regional climate model simulations to sub-kilometre scales relevant to impact applications (urban flooding, hydrology, agriculture). Accepted to the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Tackling Climate Change with Machine Learning. The work addresses a key bottleneck: as convection-permitting km-scale RCMs become feasible for multi-decade climate runs, translating their output to the sub-km scales needed for adaptation planning remains computationally prohibitive without statistical downscaling.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.22077 — Can AI Forecast the Extremes? Evaluating Probabilistic Weather Models on Tropical Cyclones: AI Beats ECMWF IFS-ENS on Track; Intensity and Ensemble Spread Remain Weak Points
items.summary: This paper benchmarks leading probabilistic AI weather models on tropical cyclone forecasting. Key findings: AI models outperform ECMWF IFS-ENS at cyclone track forecasting across multiple lead times. However, intensity forecasting and ensemble spread calibration remain weak — models underweight rare, high-intensity values via training objectives that favour large-scale atmospheric state skill. The failure modes identified here — strong track skill, weak intensity and spread — map directly onto the Typhoon Champi forecast picture on October 24: three agencies have converged on a Kyushu track, but intensity and ensemble spread at landfall remain the outstanding uncertainties.

items.headline: Mouatadid et al. in Nature: Probabilistic Bias Correction Doubles AI Subseasonal Forecast Skill at 2–6 Weeks; Improves ECMWF IFS for 92% of Temperature and 98% of Precipitation Targets; Leads SubX International Competition
items.summary: Published in Nature on October 14, this paper introduces probabilistic bias correction (PBC) as a post-processing method for AI subseasonal forecasts in the 2–6-week range. PBC doubles AI subseasonal forecast skill relative to the uncorrected AI baseline; it improves ECMWF's dynamical IFS for 92% of temperature prediction targets and 98% of precipitation targets globally; and leads the SubX international subseasonal forecast competition. This implies that existing AI weather models have substantial latent skill at subseasonal timescales masked by poorly calibrated probability distributions — significant for operational S2S forecasting and renewable energy planning applications.

items.headline: DWD AICON-Global: Germany’s Operational AI Weather Forecasting Model Completes One Year of Verification; Competitive with Operational ICON NWP for Surface Variables Short-to-Medium Range; Data Publicly Available Since March 2026
items.meta: arXiv:2608.24651 · DWD / Germany · data available since March 2026
items.summary: DWD's AICON-Global — Germany's operational AI-based deterministic global weather forecasting model — has now completed approximately one year of operational verification since data became publicly available in March 2026. The model runs on the same horizontal grid as ICON-Global (~13 km), uses the Anemoi graph neural network framework, and is initialised every three hours. Verification over the first year shows AICON performs competitively with the operational ICON NWP system for surface variables in the short to medium range. Spectral analysis confirms a damping of mesoscale activity relative to the physics-based ICON reference; precipitation skill is comparable with specific limitations noted. AICON is designed to complement, not replace, ICON in DWD's operational suite. The technical paper describing the system is arXiv:2608.24651.

items.headline: IPCC Reaches Consensus on Artificial Intelligence Guidelines for Climate Assessment at Addis Ababa Plenary; First Major IPCC Policy Decision on AI Use in Scientific Reports Amid Wider AR7 Timeline Deadlock
items.summary: Amid the broader failure to agree on the AR7 timeline, IPCC chair Jim Skea confirmed on October 19 that the Addis Ababa plenary reached agreement on guidelines for the use of artificial intelligence within IPCC scientific assessments. This marks the first time the IPCC has established formal policy on how AI-generated analysis, AI-assisted literature synthesis, or ML-based projections may be incorporated into its reports — a significant governance step given the rapid growth of ML in climate and atmospheric science. The broader AR7 timeline dispute — Saudi Arabia and India backing 2029 vs. EU and AOSIS wanting 2028 — remains unresolved.

items.title: Applied Digital and Soluna Holdings Sign Definitive Agreement for 50 MW AI Data Centre Adjacent to 150 MW Briscoe Wind Farm, Texas; Wind + Grid Hybrid Power for AI Compute Colocation
items.body_html: Applied Digital Corporation and Soluna Holdings signed a definitive agreement on approximately 22 October to jointly develop a 50 MW AI data centre in Briscoe County, Texas, co-located with the 150 MW Briscoe Wind Farm. Power supply will mix wind generation with grid electricity to absorb curtailment while delivering firm AI compute capacity. The deal is one of a growing wave of AI infrastructure projects seeking co-location with renewable assets to reduce grid interconnect costs and carbon intensity — a strategy with direct implications for wind farm economics as curtailment rates rise.

items.title: AMEA Power Signs 250 MW/1,000 MWh Battery Storage Project Agreements for Uzbekistan’s Bukhara Region; Central Asia’s Largest Battery Commitment of 2026; Executed at Tashkent Energy Sector Investors’ Council 16 Oct
items.body_html: AMEA Power signed project agreements on 16 October for a 250 MW/1,000 MWh BESS in Uzbekistan’s Bukhara region (Gijduvan district), announced publicly 20 October at the Tashkent Energy Sector Investors’ Council. The deal adds to AMEA Power’s existing 150 MW/300 MWh Tashkent system (ground broken May 2026), bringing total committed Uzbekistan storage to 400 MW/1,300 MWh. No deal price was disclosed.

items.title: XCF Global Completes All-Stock Three-Way Merger Combining Renewable Fuel Production, Biomass-to-Fuels Development (Southern Energy Renewables) and Environmental Asset Monetisation (DevvStream); Integrated Lifecycle Platform for Biomass-Based Fuels and Carbon Credits
items.body_html: XCF Global completed an all-stock three-way business combination on 19 October, merging renewable fuel production with Southern Energy Renewables’ biomass-to-fuels pipeline and DevvStream’s carbon-asset monetisation platform. The combined entity targets the full value chain of biomass-based fuel projects from production through carbon credit generation. No deal terms were disclosed.
